To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the most common cause of accidents in the medical accelerator is human error; 2) the most common type of human error is the failure to follow established procedures, and 3) the most important safety feature of a medical accelerator is an operator who follows procedures.

(1) a comprehensive safety program must be in place for all medical accelerators and (2) the safety program should include a thorough training program, a quality assurance program, a detailed emergency response plan, and a detailed written procedure for equipment malfunction.

(1) the most common causes of equipment failure in medical accelerators are mechanical and electrical in nature, (2) equipment malfunctions are often the result of improper operation, (3) equipment malfunctions may result in patient injury, and (4) a comprehensive safety program is needed to minimize the consequences of equipment failure

the safe and effective utilization of medical accelerators in a radiation therapy environment.
the safe operation of medical accelerators.

the safety of patients and staff should be a primary concern of every user of a medical accelerator.
